mainTopic: The fixed tithing times for מעשר בהמה, the disputes over their dates and the new year, and בן עזאי's rule for אלול-born animals
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer. The fixed tithing times (גרנות) for מעשר בהמה exist so that animals will be available for עולי רגלים, because owners like to do the מצוה first and sell afterward. The גמרא explains that the time is called a גורן because it makes the animals טבל, like grain on a threshing floor. It then defines רבי עקיבא's word פרס as fifteen days, which is half of the thirty days of studying הלכות פסח. Next it explains the dates of בן עזאי (כ״ט אדר, א׳ סיון, כ״ט אב) and of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון (א׳ ניסן, א׳ סיון, כ״ט אלול), with a reason for each. The dispute about whether the year for animal tithe begins in אלול (רבי מאיר) or תשרי leads בן עזאי to tithe אלול-born animals as their own group. רבי יוחנן explains that בן עזאי could not settle the dispute by logic, because both sides relied on traditions from חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי. A ברייתא and a משנה teach that only a new year separates animals, while the tithing seasons do not. The amud ends as רבא begins a case of animals born in אב, אלול, and תשרי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Fixed tithing times keep animals available for pilgrims
steps.stepSummary: The reason for the fixed animal-tithing times is so that there will be plenty of animals for עולי רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that animals will be available for those going up to ירושלים for the רגלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to a question asked on the previous amud: why did the רבנן set fixed times for מעשר בהמה? It answers that this makes sure animals are available for people coming to the רגלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tithing times fall shortly before each רגל. Owners will hold on to their animals until it is time to tithe them. So right before the רגל, there are many animals available to sell to pilgrims for food or קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: people going up to ירושלים for the three Festivals

phrases.english: So that animals will be readily available
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer whose question appears on the previous amud.

phrases.english: for those ascending for the pilgrimage Festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא בְּהֵמָה מְצוּיָה לְעוֹלֵי רְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question (earlier) about why the גרנות were set.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fixed times exist so that animals will be available for pilgrims at each רגל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the purpose of the whole system of גרנות. The rest of this passage is built on that purpose.

steps.title: But the משנה allows selling before the tithing time
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that before the גורן you may sell and slaughter animals. That seems to defeat the purpose just given.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though we learned in the משנה: before the tithing time arrives, it is permitted to sell and slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a problem with the reason it just gave. If the משנה lets you sell or slaughter animals before the tithing time, why would the fixed times keep animals around? This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason in Step 1 only works if owners keep their animals until the tithing time. But the משנה says nothing forces them to wait. So it looks like the fixed times would not actually keep animals available.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'threshing floor'; here, the fixed time for tithing animals
permitted to sell and to slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a separate argument that stands on its own. The sentence runs straight into the answer in the next step. The גמרא raises the problem and solves it in a single sentence.

phrases.english: And even though we learned in the Mishnah:
Until the time designated for gathering has arrived
it is permitted to sell and slaughter the animals

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that fixed tithing times keep animals available for pilgrims
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Owners are allowed to sell or slaughter before the גורן. So nothing makes them hold on to the animals, and the stated purpose seems to fail.

steps.title: People prefer to do the מצוה first
steps.stepSummary: Even though selling early is allowed, a person prefers to do the מצוה of מעשר with his animals first and sell or eat them afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person is pleased to have a מצוה done with his money, and afterward to sell and eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. Owners are allowed to sell early, but they usually choose to wait so they can do the מצוה of מעשר בהמה first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on how people actually behave, not on what they are forced to do. Since owners want to do the מצוה, they naturally hold on to their animals until the גורן. That keeps a supply ready right before each רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: it is pleasing to him, he prefers
a מצוה done with his own property

steps.whatToRemember: The fixed tithing times work because people want to do the מצוה first, not because the law forces them to keep their animals. That is why animals end up available for pilgrims.

phrases.english: he prefers that a מצוה be done with his money,
and afterward to sell and eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in Step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical human behavior rather than legal obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since selling early is allowed, owners would sell early and the fixed times would accomplish nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Owners choose to wait and tithe first because they value the מצוה. So animals are available near each רגל.

steps.title: Why is the tithing time called a threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא uses the word גורן for the animal-tithing time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does he call it a 'גורן'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a word question: why is a time for tithing animals called a 'threshing floor'? This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גורן normally refers to the place where grain is gathered and threshed. Using that word for an animal-tithing time looks strange, so the גמרא asks for the reason.

phrases.english: And why does he call it goren (threshing floor)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to explaining a term from the משנה quoted in Step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the animal-tithing time is called a גורן

steps.title: The tithing time creates obligation like a threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: The tithing time makes the animals טבל, just as gathering grain on the threshing floor makes produce obligated in מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it makes them טבל, like a threshing floor does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the name. Once the tithing time arrives, the animals have the status of untithed produce, just like grain once it reaches the threshing floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With grain, reaching the גורן is the point when the obligation to tithe begins. In the same way, once the animal גורן arrives, you may not slaughter the animals until you tithe them. Before that time, you could.

keyTerms.meaning: that it makes it טבל (untithed and forbidden)
produce from which the required tithes have not yet been taken

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why selling and slaughtering are allowed before the גורן but forbidden after it. The גורן is the moment the obligation begins.

phrases.english: Because it renders the animals untithed like a threshing floor does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tithing time creates the obligation to tithe, just as the threshing floor does for grain.

steps.title: How long is פרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long the time called פרס is, the word רבי עקיבא uses for the tithing times before the רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'פרס'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about another word from the משנה. רבי עקיבא said the tithing times are at the פרס of each רגל. How long a period is that? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא places the גרנות at the פרס of פסח, עצרת, and סוכות. Without knowing how long a פרס is, nobody would know when the tithing time actually starts.

keyTerms.meaning: a period just before a Festival (literally 'half')

phrases.english: And how much is 'adjacent' (peras)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about a different word in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of the period called פרס

steps.title: פרס is no less than fifteen days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה explains that a פרס is at least fifteen days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה explained: a פרס is not less than fifteen days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives the length: a פרס is at least fifteen days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So according to רבי עקיבא, the animal tithing time falls about fifteen days before each רגל. That gives owners enough time to tithe their animals and still sell them to pilgrims before the Festival.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה, a תנא

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, each tithing time is at the פרס of a רגל, which means about fifteen days before it.
steps.confusionAlert: פרס literally means 'half'. Fifteen days is half of the thirty days before פסח during which one studies הלכות פסח (as the גמרא will soon show). It does not mean 'any time close to' the Festival.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, explained:
Peras is not less
than fifteen days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פרס is at least fifteen days.

steps.title: How do we know a פרס is fifteen days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the word פרס means fifteen days.
steps.simpleTranslation: What shows this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that the word פרס means fifteen days, as רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה just said. This question sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 gave a number, but not a reason. Now the גמרא wants to know what in the word פרס itself points to fifteen days.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows this? What is the source?

phrases.english: From where is this inferred?
phrases.notes: Asking for the source of 'פרס = fifteen days'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the definition given in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the word פרס shows that it means fifteen days?

steps.title: פרס means half
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the word פרס means 'half.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: 'פרוס' means half.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers that פרס means 'half' (like a פרוסה, a piece broken off). This is only part of the answer, because we still need to know half of what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word now has a meaning: half. But 'half' alone does not give us fifteen days. That gap leads straight into the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A portion or half, like a broken piece

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
'Peros' means half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by defining the word.

steps.title: Half of what?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what period פרס is half of.
steps.simpleTranslation: Half of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what larger period פרס is half of. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To reach fifteen days, the 'whole' must be thirty days. The גמרא needs to name that thirty-day period.

phrases.english: Half of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי אבהו's definition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the whole period that פרס is half of?

steps.title: Half of the thirty days of studying הלכות פסח
steps.stepSummary: פרס is half of the thirty days before פסח when one studies הלכות פסח. Half of thirty is fifteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Half of the time for studying הלכות פסח, as a ברייתא teaches: we ask and teach הלכות פסח for thirty days before פסח. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: two weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole period is the thirty days before פסח, when people learn הלכות פסח. Half of thirty is fifteen, so a פרס is fifteen days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses the first opinion in the ברייתא: thirty days of study before פסח. Half of that period is fifteen days, which matches רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view of two weeks is not part of this proof, but the גמרא uses it later (Step 21) to explain why רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון tithe on א׳ ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: We ask about and teach (the laws)

steps.confusionAlert: The fifteen days come from the first opinion (thirty days). They do not come from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's two weeks.
steps.whatToRemember: פרס = half of the thirty days of studying הלכות פסח = fifteen days.

phrases.english: Half of the time for the laws of Passover,
as it is taught in a baraita:
One asks about and teaches the laws of Passover
thirty days before Passover.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Two weeks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 and supports the answer with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Half of the thirty-day study period before פסח, which is fifteen days.

steps.title: Quoting בן עזאי's dates from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בן עזאי's fixed dates: כ״ט אדר and א׳ סיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי says: on the twenty-ninth of אדר, and on the first of סיון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes בן עזאי's opinion from the משנה. This step opens a new topic and sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gave a span of time ('a פרס before the רגל'). בן עזאי gives exact calendar dates. This difference is what the גמרא will examine.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argues with רבי עקיבא in the משנה

phrases.english: Ben Azzai says:
On the twenty-ninth of Adar, on the first of Sivan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining פרס to בן עזאי's opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן עזאי sets the tithing times on fixed dates: כ״ט אדר and א׳ סיון (and כ״ט אב).

steps.title: What is the dispute about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the difference between רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי. This sets up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fifteen days before פסח lands at the very end of אדר, which is close to בן עזאי's כ״ט אדר. So the גמרא wants to know why רבי עקיבא would not just name a fixed date.

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וּבֶן עַזַּאי?
phrases.english: About what do Rabbi Akiva and ben Azzai disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reason behind the opinion quoted in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What underlying issue divides רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי about the אדר date?

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: אדר varies in length
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that אדר is sometimes 30 days and sometimes 29, so he cannot give one fixed date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds: the אדר next to ניסן is sometimes full and sometimes short. So sometimes the day falls on the thirtieth, and sometimes on the twenty-ninth. That is why he does not set a fixed date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא's view. Since אדר can be 29 or 30 days, 'fifteen days before פסח' lands on different dates in different years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Count fifteen days back from ט״ו ניסן. In a full אדר you land on ל׳ אדר. In a short אדר you land on כ״ט אדר. Since no single date always works, רבי עקיבא describes the time by counting days instead.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not set a fixed date

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
The Adar adjacent to Nisan
is sometimes full and sometimes short;
sometimes it (the fifteenth day back) falls on the thirtieth
and sometimes it falls on the twenty-ninth;

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא קְבִיעַ לֵיהּ זְמַן.
phrases.english: and therefore he does not fix a date for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the answer to Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא holds that אדר's length varies, so the date shifts and cannot be fixed.

steps.title: בן עזאי: אדר is always short
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי holds that the אדר before ניסן always has 29 days, so he can set the date at כ״ט אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בן עזאי holds: the אדר next to ניסן is always short. Therefore he sets a fixed date: the twenty-ninth of אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains בן עזאי's side. He holds that אדר always has 29 days, so fifteen days before פסח is always כ״ט אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים actually agree on fifteen days before פסח. They differ only about the calendar. If אדר is always short, the date never shifts, so בן עזאי can name it.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute over אדר is about the calendar, not about how far before פסח to tithe. Both mean fifteen days before.

phrases.english: And ben Azzai holds:
The Adar adjacent to Nisan is always short;
therefore he fixes a date for it
on the twenty-ninth of Adar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to Step 13 with בן עזאי's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בן עזאי holds that אדר is always 29 days, so כ״ט אדר is always fifteen days before פסח.

steps.title: Why בן עזאי tithes only on the first of סיון
steps.stepSummary: Fewer animals are born before שבועות. If they were tithed fifteen days early, they would all be sold before the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first of סיון: since there are not many animals, if you say he should tithe earlier, by the time the רגל arrives they will all be gone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why בן עזאי does not use fifteen days before שבועות, and instead picks א׳ סיון, only a few days before. Fewer animals are born in this period, so tithing early would leave nothing left for the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal of the tithing times is to have animals ready for the pilgrims. With a small herd, tithing fifteen days early means everything gets sold or eaten before שבועות. Tithing close to the רגל keeps animals available.

phrases.english: On the first of Sivan —
phrases.notes: Quoting בן עזאי's words from the משנה

phrases.english: since they (the animals) are not many,
if you say he should tithe earlier,
by the time the Festival arrives they will be finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second date in בן עזאי's list and answers an implied question about it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With few animals, tithing early would leave none for שבועות, so he tithes close to the רגל.

steps.title: כ״ט אב: בן עזאי follows his own view about אלול
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי picks כ״ט אב because he holds that animals born in אלול are tithed as their own separate group.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the twenty-ninth of אב, etc. בן עזאי follows his own reasoning, for he said: animals born in אלול are tithed by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why בן עזאי's last date is כ״ט אב and not fifteen days before סוכות. He holds elsewhere that animals born in אלול form their own group, so the tithing must happen before אלול begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a doubt whether the new year for animal tithing is א׳ אלול or א׳ תשרי. So בן עזאי keeps the אלול-born animals separate, to avoid mixing animals of two years. Tithing on the last day of אב gathers everything before אלול starts.

keyTerms.meaning: Are tithed as a separate group

steps.whatToRemember: Each of בן עזאי's dates has its own reason: אדר (the calendar), סיון (few animals), אב (אלול-born animals are a separate group).
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that בן עזאי's dates are not random. Each one comes from a principle he holds elsewhere about the tithing year.

phrases.english: On the twenty-ninth of Av, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: Ben Azzai follows his own reasoning,
as he said:
Those born in Elul are tithed by themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third date in בן עזאי's list, after the סיון date in Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since אלול-born animals are tithed separately, the tithing must happen before אלול, on כ״ט אב.

steps.title: Why not tithe on the thirtieth of אב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בן עזאי. If his goal is to tithe at the very end of the group born before אלול, he could pick the 30th of אב, which comes later than כ״ט אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let him tithe them on the thirtieth day of אב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on בן עזאי's choice of כ״ט אב. It asks why he does not wait one more day, to the 30th.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי wants to tithe the animals born up to the end of אב as one group, because animals born in אלול are tithed separately. The 30th of אב looks like the most natural last day for that group. So the גמרא asks why he stops one day early.

phrases.english: But let him tithe them on the thirtieth day!
phrases.notes: This means the 30th of אב, the last possible day before אלול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the date of כ״ט אב given in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן עזאי's choice of כ״ט אב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the cutoff is the end of אב, then the 30th of אב is a better and later date. Choosing the 29th seems to leave out one day for no reason.

steps.title: אב is sometimes short, and new and old animals must be kept apart
steps.stepSummary: Sometimes אב has only 29 days, so the '30th day' would really be א׳ אלול. Tithing on that day would mix the new animals born in אלול with the old ones born in אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes they make אב a short month, and we need to make a clear separation between the new animals and the old ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. בן עזאי picks the 29th because it is the only day that is always still inside אב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In those times the length of a month could change, so the 30th day might already be the first day of אלול. According to בן עזאי, animals born in אלול are a new group. The tithing therefore has to happen on a day that is surely still in the old period, which keeps the new and old animals clearly apart.

keyTerms.meaning: They make it short (a month of 29 days)
New and old (animals from different tithing years)

phrases.english: Sometimes they make Av a short month,
phrases.notes: Then the 30th day is really א׳ אלול.

phrases.english: and we need to make a clear separation
between the new and the old.
phrases.notes: New means born in אלול; old means born in אב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 30th of אב is always still part of אב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 30th may be א׳ אלול, so only the 29th is surely still in the old period.
steps.whatToRemember: בן עזאי sets the date at כ״ט אב so the animals born in אלול are never mixed with the earlier group.

steps.title: The משנה quotes the dates of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns to the third opinion in the משנה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון give the dates as א׳ ניסן, א׳ סיון, and so on.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: on the first of ניסן, on the first of סיון, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the next steps, which explain each date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new section. Earlier the גמרא explained רבי עקיבא and בן עזאי. Now it will explain why רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון chose their three dates.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנאים who hold the third opinion in the משנה
And so on (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
On the first of Nisan, on the first of Sivan, etc.
phrases.notes: The third date, כ״ט אלול, is covered by the 'etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בן עזאי to the next opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three tithing dates are א׳ ניסן, א׳ סיון, and כ״ט אלול.

steps.title: Explaining א׳ ניסן and א׳ סיון
steps.stepSummary: א׳ ניסן follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says we study הלכות פסח for two weeks before פסח. א׳ סיון uses the same reason we gave for בן עזאי, which is that fewer animals are born before שבועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first of ניסן follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who says two weeks. The first of סיון is as we said before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first two dates of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון. Both reasons rely on ideas the גמרא already used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: א׳ ניסן is two weeks before פסח, which matches רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'two weeks' of preparation. א׳ סיון is closer to שבועות because fewer animals are born in that season. Tithing earlier would leave too few animals, as the גמרא explained for בן עזאי in Step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who says the study of הלכות פסח begins two weeks before פסח

phrases.english: On the first of Nisan —
in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
who says: two weeks.
phrases.notes: Two weeks before פסח.

phrases.english: On the first of Sivan — as we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 16: fewer animals are born before שבועות.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first two dates quoted in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון chose א׳ ניסן and א׳ סיון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: א׳ ניסן follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's two weeks. א׳ סיון follows the earlier reasoning about fewer births.

steps.title: Explaining כ״ט אלול
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון choose כ״ט אלול because they hold that א׳ תשרי is the new year for מעשר בהמה. So all of אלול still belongs to the old year.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the twenty-ninth of אלול: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון follow their own view, since they say the first of תשרי is the new year for מעשר בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third date. It is based on these תנאים' general view about when the year for animal tithe begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי is unsure which year אלול belongs to, so he keeps אלול-born animals as a separate group and tithes before אלול, on כ״ט אב. For רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the new year only starts on א׳ תשרי, so all of אלול is the old year. That is why they tithe at the very end of אלול, the last day of the old year.

keyTerms.meaning: The new year for animal tithe

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. For בן עזאי the cutoff comes before אלול. For רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, all of אלול is still the old year.

phrases.english: On the twenty-ninth of Elul —
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon follow their reasoning,
for they say: on the first of Tishrei
is the new year for animal tithe.
phrases.notes: Animals born before this date and animals born after it cannot be tithed together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the dates in Step 20 by covering the third one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the third date is כ״ט אלול.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the new year for מעשר בהמה is א׳ תשרי, the last day before it is used.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument over the third date comes from a deeper argument about when the year for animal tithe begins.

steps.title: The משנה: not א׳ תשרי because it is יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's own reason for choosing כ״ט אלול instead of א׳ תשרי. The reason is that א׳ תשרי is a יום טוב (ראש השנה), when tithing is not done.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they say the twenty-ninth of אלול and not the first of תשרי? Because it is a יום טוב, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the reason the משנה itself gives. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה explains that the date was moved one day earlier because one cannot tithe animals on יום טוב. The גמרא brings this line so it can question whether the reason is really needed.

phrases.english: And why did they say on the twenty-ninth of Elul,
and did not say on the first of Tishrei?
Because it is a Festival, etc.
phrases.notes: Animals are not tithed on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה's reason for the date explained in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tithing date is כ״ט אלול and not א׳ תשרי, because א׳ תשרי is יום טוב.

steps.title: Why not use the need to separate new and old animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the יום טוב reason. Tithing on א׳ תשרי is already ruled out, because it would mix the new year's animals with the old year's animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it derive this from the fact that we need to make a clear separation between new and old animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason the משנה gave. It points out that a simpler reason already explains the date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: א׳ תשרי is the start of the new year, so animals born on that day are 'new'. Tithing on that day would mix new animals with old ones, which is the same problem as in Step 19. So the יום טוב reason seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it derive it instead from

phrases.english: But let it derive it
phrases.notes: This is the beginning of a challenge.

phrases.english: from the fact that we need to make a clear separation
between the new and the old!
phrases.notes: New means born in תשרי; old means born in אלול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason quoted in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's יום טוב reason for not tithing on א׳ תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: א׳ תשרי is already ruled out because it is the first day of the new year. Tithing then would mix new and old animals, so the יום טוב reason seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The משנה gives one reason and then adds another
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's main reason is to keep the new animals apart from the old ones. It adds a second reason: א׳ תשרי is יום טוב, and you cannot mark animals with paint on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one reason and then adds another. The first reason is that we must keep the new animals apart from the old ones. The extra reason is that it is יום טוב, and you cannot tithe on יום טוב because of the red marking paint.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 24. The משנה is not relying only on the יום טוב reason. It gives two reasons together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 asked why the יום טוב reason is needed if mixing years already rules out א׳ תשרי. The answer is that the mixing problem is the main reason, and יום טוב is an added point. On יום טוב you cannot paint the tenth animal with סקרתא, so tithing that day cannot work anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: It says one reason and adds another
New and old (this year's and last year's animals)
Red paint used to mark every tenth animal

steps.whatToRemember: כ״ט אלול is chosen for two reasons: to keep the years apart, and because א׳ תשרי is יום טוב, when marking with paint is not allowed.

phrases.english: It states one reason and another
One: that we need to make a distinction
between the new and the old animals
And another: because it is a Festival
and it is impossible to tithe on a Festival
because of the red marking paint
phrases.notes: Painting is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two reasons together: a main reason plus an added one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יום טוב reason seemed unnecessary
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists the mixing problem first and adds the יום טוב reason as a second reason

steps.title: The משנה's opinions of רבי מאיר and בן עזאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. רבי מאיר says א׳ אלול is the new year for מעשר בהמה, and then the משנה brings בן עזאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: The first of אלול is the new year for tithing animals. בן עזאי says, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה to discuss a new part of it. This sets up the explanation of בן עזאי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר puts the new year one month earlier than רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, who say א׳ תשרי. Because of this gap, it is unclear which year the animals born in אלול belong to. That question is what בן עזאי deals with.

keyTerms.meaning: New year for the animal tithe
And so on (the quote is cut short)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
On the first of Elul is the new year
for the animal tithe.
Ben Azzai says, and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: בְּאֶחָד בֶּאֱלוּל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new section of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר holds that א׳ אלול is the new year for מעשר בהמה

steps.title: A ברייתא explains בן עזאי's reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows why בן עזאי rules this way. Since the sages disagree, the animals born in אלול are tithed as a separate group.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: בן עזאי said, since these sages say this and those sages say that, the animals born in אלול are tithed by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the reason for בן עזאי's opinion. He is unsure which side is right, so he keeps the אלול animals separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, אלול animals belong to the new year. According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, they belong to the old year. Because of this doubt, they cannot be mixed with either year, so they form their own group for tithing.

phrases.english: It is taught: Ben Azzai said:
Since these say this,
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: א׳ תשרי

phrases.english: and those say that,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר: א׳ אלול

phrases.english: the Elul-born animals are tithed by themselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי: הוֹאִיל וְהַלָּלוּ אוֹמְרִים כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the בן עזאי opinion quoted in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the doubt, animals born in אלול are tithed as a separate group

steps.title: Why doesn't בן עזאי just decide who is right?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: instead of leaving it as a doubt, בן עזאי should check whose reasoning makes more sense and rule that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him look at whose reasoning makes more sense!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בן עזאי's approach. A sage should weigh the reasons and choose one side, not stay in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the idea of staying in doubt at all. If the dispute rests on reasoning, a great sage could examine it and decide. Then there would be no need for a separate אלול group.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes more sense / is more logical

phrases.english: But let him see the reasoning
of whom is more logical!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of Step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: בן עזאי's choice to treat the dispute as a doubt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sage should decide the dispute by weighing the reasons, so there should be no doubt

steps.title: בן עזאי was sharp enough to decide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the reply that בן עזאי could not figure out their reasoning. It brings a ברייתא where בן עזאי says all the sages seem to him like garlic peel, except רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he was not able to understand their reasoning, but it was taught: בן עזאי says, all the sages of Israel seem to me like a garlic peel, except for this bald one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its challenge stronger. It proves that בן עזאי was brilliant, so he could surely have judged between the opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might defend בן עזאי by saying the reasoning was too hard for him. The ברייתא shows he viewed nearly every sage as far below him. Such a person should have been able to decide, so the question from Step 28 stands even stronger.
steps.confusionAlert: "The bald one" refers to רבי עקיבא, בן עזאי's teacher. This is not an insult. בן עזאי is praising רבי עקיבא as the only one greater than himself.

phrases.english: And if you would say: he is not able
to grasp their reasoning,
but it is taught: Ben Azzai says:
All the Sages of Israel seem to me
like a garlic peel
except for this bald one!
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לָא מָצֵי קָאֵי אַטַּעְמַיְיהוּ, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the קשיא of Step 28 by blocking a possible defense
steps.raayaObject: That בן עזאי was able to judge the sages' reasoning
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which בן עזאי calls all the sages garlic peel except רבי עקיבא

steps.title: The dispute comes from tradition, not from logic
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that both opinions were passed down as a tradition from חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי. Logic cannot decide between two traditions, so בן עזאי had to treat it as a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They said it from tradition, from the mouths of חגי, זכריה, and מלאכי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Brilliance does not help here, because this dispute is about which tradition is true, not about reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side said it had received its date as a tradition (שמועה) from the last נביאים. You cannot use logic to find out which report is accurate. So even בן עזאי had to stay in doubt and tithe the אלול animals separately.
steps.whatToRemember: בן עזאי kept the אלול animals separate not because he lacked understanding. Both opinions were traditions, and logic cannot decide between traditions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule: when a dispute is about a received tradition, reasoning cannot settle it, and we must act according to the doubt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
They said it from tradition,
from the mouths of Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפִּי הַשְּׁמוּעָה אֲמָרוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 28 and 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the nature of the dispute: tradition, not reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute is about reasoning, so a brilliant sage could decide it
steps.terutzMaskana: Each side relied on a tradition from the נביאים, so logic cannot decide, and the doubt remains

steps.title: A ברייתא shows how בן עזאי's rule works
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives examples. Animals born in אלול do not join with those born in אב or in תשרי. Animals born in תשרי and the following אב do join.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: How did בן עזאי mean that animals born in אלול are tithed by themselves? If a person had five born in אב and five in אלול, they do not join together. Five in אלול and five in תשרי also do not join. But five in תשרי and five in אב do join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives real examples of בן עזאי's rule that animals born in אלול are tithed as a separate group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You need ten animals from the same year to give מעשר. אלול might be the end of the old year (if the year starts in תשרי) or the start of the new year (if the year starts in אלול, as רבי מאיר says). So אלול animals cannot safely join either side. But תשרי through the following אב is one year according to both opinions, so those animals join.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
They are tithed by themselves, as a separate group
They join together to make up the count of ten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that תשרי and אב are far apart, so they can't join. Count forward from תשרי to the next אב. That whole stretch is inside one year according to both opinions.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: בְּאֵיזֶה צַד אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי
phrases.english: It was taught: In what way did ben Azzai say
that the Elul-born animals are tithed by themselves?
If five were born to him in Av
and five in Elul, they do not combine
phrases.notes: Elul might already be the new year, according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה בֶּאֱלוּל וַחֲמִשָּׁה בְּתִשְׁרִי — אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין,
phrases.english: five in Elul and five in Tishrei, they do not combine
phrases.notes: Tishrei might be the new year, according to the other opinion.

phrases.english: five in Tishrei and five in Av do combine.
phrases.notes: This means the אב that comes after that תשרי.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: בְּאֵיזֶה צַד אָמַר בֶּן עַזַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the reason for בן עזאי's doubt is settled, the גמרא shows how his rule works in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלול animals join with neither אב nor תשרי animals. תשרי animals join with the following אב animals.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to teach the last case, that תשרי and אב animals join.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If תשרי and the following אב are clearly in the same year, why say it at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling seems to follow directly from בן עזאי's own reasoning. So the ברייתא looks like it is teaching nothing new. The גמרא is about to explain what the new point is.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. This is a challenge that asks what new point is being taught.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: A one-word challenge. It stands alone because it is the whole question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last case of the ברייתא from step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that animals from תשרי and the following אב join together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Those months are clearly in the same year by both opinions, so the ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The tithing seasons do not split the animals
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought that the set tithing seasons (גרנות) split animals into groups, just as years do. The ברייתא teaches that they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: just as years separate animals, the tithing seasons also separate them. So the ברייתא teaches us that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing what mistake the ברייתא is preventing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are set times during the year for gathering animals to tithe them (גרנות). Between תשרי and אב, some of these seasons pass. Someone might think each season closes off a separate group. The ברייתא teaches that only the change of year separates animals, not the tithing seasons.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a wrong idea that the teaching comes to block.
They separate, they break the group apart
The set seasons for gathering animals to tithe them (literally 'threshing floors')
It teaches us (that the wrong idea is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: Here גֳּרָנוֹת does not mean grain threshing floors. It means the set times in the year for tithing animals.

phrases.english: You might have said
that just as years separate
the gathering seasons also separate
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge from step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the hidden new point (חידוש) by naming a wrong idea the teaching blocks
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The tithing seasons separate animals into groups, just like a change of year does.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a change of year separates animals. The tithing seasons do not.

steps.title: A משנה supports this answer
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules the same way: animals born before and after ראש השנה do not join, but animals born before and after a tithing season do join.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in the משנה: Five born before ראש השנה and five after ראש השנה do not join. Five born before the tithing season and five after it do join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by quoting a משנה that says the same thing outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly separates the two ideas. A new year breaks up the group, but a tithing season does not. This confirms the point that the ברייתא was teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The new year for animal tithes

steps.whatToRemember: For מעשר בהמה, only a new year splits animals into separate groups. The tithing seasons never do. בן עזאי keeps אלול animals separate only because we are unsure which year אלול belongs to.

phrases.english: As we learned: five before Rosh HaShana

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲמִשָּׁה לְאַחַר רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה — אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין,
phrases.english: and five after Rosh HaShana do not combine
five before the gathering season

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲמִשָּׁה לְאַחַר הַגּוֹרֶן — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.english: and five after the gathering season do combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the answer given in step 33.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that tithing seasons do not separate animals, while new years do
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about animals born before and after ראש השנה and before and after the גורן

steps.title: רבא starts a case with animals born in three months
steps.stepSummary: רבא describes a case according to בן עזאי: five animals born in אב, five in אלול, and five in תשרי, all brought into the pen to be tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: According to בן עזאי, if five were born to a person in אב, five in אלול, and five in תשרי, he brings them all into the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting up a new, more complicated case. His ruling continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three groups. אב and תשרי are in different years for sure. אלול is uncertain and could belong to either side. רבא will explain how to tithe this mixed group according to בן עזאי's doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A pen for animals, where they are counted for tithing

phrases.english: Rava said: According to ben Azzai
if five were born to him in Av
and five in Elul and five in Tishrei
he gathers them into the pen to be tithed
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's examples with a more complex three-month case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup: according to בן עזאי, the animals from אב, אלול, and תשרי are brought into the pen together for tithing. The ruling continues on the next amud.
